newsitem.title: SYRIA: Iran defence minister backs Syria on edge of Golan.
newsitem.headline: Iran defence minister backs Syria on edge of Golan.

text.p: Iranian Defence Minister Mohammad Forouzandeh backed Syria's "heroic positions" during a visit on Friday to the edge of the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights, Iranian officials said.

They said he expressed hope during a visit to the ruins of Quneitra, a city destroyed by Israel, that Syria would secure the return of the plateau that it lost to Israel during the 1967 Middle East war.
"Iran supports Syria's heroic positions and backs it in its confrontation with the ugly Israeli aggressions," one official quoted Forouzadeh as saying.
Syria held sporadic peace talks with Israel from 1991 until negotiations, stalemated over the future of the Golan, were broken off last March.
Israel returned Quneitra and some other parts of the Golan in June 1974 under a U.S-brokered deal that followed its 1973 war with Syria.
Officials said the Iranian minister, who arrived in Damascus on Thursday, would discuss ways to increase military cooperation between Syria and Iran. Official talks would start on Saturday.

The visit, at the invitation of Syrian Defence Minister Lieutentant General Mustafa Tlas, was aimed at "discussing various military issues but no arms deals or military agreements would be tackled during the talks," an official said.
"The timing of the visit is aimed at showing Israel and the United States which is hosting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Syria was not alone," an Iranian diplomat said.

Other diplomats noted the visit came amid increased tension between Israel and the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) in south Lebanon. It follows reports that Iran was sending missiles to Hizbollah fighters through Damascus.
Syria and Iran back Hizbollah fighters in their war against Israeli troops who occupy a strip of south Lebanon to prevent guerrillas reaching Israel.
Both also back militant Palestinian groups, including Hamas and the Islamic Jihad who claimed several suicide attacks in Israel that killed scores of people.
Syria has had close ties with Tehran since the Islamic revolution in 1979 and backed Iran in its war with Iraq between 1980 and 1988.
